newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS - New Alusuisse CEO seeks globalisation.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - New Alusuisse CEO seeks globalisation.

text.p: Sergio Marchionne, the Canadian named on Tuesday to take over the helm of Alusuisse-Lonza, aims to turn the Swiss-based packaging, aluminium and chemicals group into a global concern.

Marchionne, 44, who will rise to chief executive from chief financial officer next April, said major strategic changes are not expected, but he is looking for ways to grow by using the existing skills in the group's three core activities.
"There is an overriding direction of the group and that is to...turn ourselves into a global industrial house," he said in an interview.
The rise of Marchionne to the top of Alusuisse took only two years, but his ascendency hardly surprised analysts.

"Marchionne is the right man," said Werner Richli at CS Research in Zurich. "He is relatively young, dynamic, very unconvetional and has a lot of drive. He has a lot of toughness and sees things from a financial point of view," Richli said.
Analysts said Marchionne would bring continuity and an international financial perspective when he succeeds Theodor Tschopp, 59, at the shareholders' meeting on April 2.
A heavy investment programme by Alusuisse over the next few years will put the company in a strong cash position by 1997, a situation that can be used to advance the group further.
Marchionne said the company's forecast for 1996 net profit to exceed 1995's 385 million Swiss francs ($303 million) -- up 86 percent from the previous year -- still held true.
He joined Alusuisse in 1994 from Canadian packaging group Lawson Mardon, which was acquired by Alusuisse as part of its move to diversify away from aluminium and chemicals.
Marchionne, who moved from Italy to Canada when he was 14 years old, said his first task will be to learn German. Alusuisse is based in the German-speaking part of Swizterland.
He said he did not see any major strategic changes and added he would be careful not to spread the group too wide.
"It will be a geographical diversification of know-how within a clearly defined set of core competencies," he said.

As an example of Alusuisse's globalisation, Marchionne pointed to a $30 million joint venture in China, where its chemical subsidiary Lonza Ltd will produce vitamin B3 for the animal feed industry, which is growing as fast as the Chinese appetite for meat.

The current strategy is to allow each of Alusuisse's three divisions to establish what Marchionne called "defensible long-term positions" in the market along with making the greatest possible value for the group.

Asked about speculation that its aluminium activities will be combined with another company, Marchionne said there were no such plans, but it would also be premature for him to speculate on changes to Alusuisse's corporate structure.

Plans to change Alusuisse's name to reflect that it is more than just an aluminium producer have also been put on ice. "I am not sure there is any value in pursuing that," he said. ($1=1.2712 Swiss Franc)
